(1) it is possible to determine the structure of a protein crystal by electron crystallographic methods; (2) the structure of a single protein crystal can be determined from a single electron diffraction pattern; (3) a structure determination can be carried out without any knowledge of the protein's structure; (4) it is not necessary to use heavy atoms to solve a structure; (5) it is possible, in principle, to determine a structure directly from an electron micrograph of a

1) the electron crystallographer can use the electron diffraction data from a crystal to extend the basis phase set to the higher-resolution data; 2) the multisolution approach can be used to determine the phases for a low-resolution data set from a negatively-stated membrane protein crystal.
it is possible to obtain the phases for electron diffraction patterns from electron micrographs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for solving the phase problem in electron crystallograph of proteins.
the application of direct phase determination methods to electron micrographs and electron diffraction patterns.
the application of the direct methods approach to the structure determination of biological macromolecules by electron crystallographic techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Sayre equation can be used for electron crystallographic phase determination.
the electron crystallographer is now in a position to determine the structure of protein crystals by electron diffraction and microscopy, without the need for a priori knowledge of the structure.
the electron crystallographer is in a position to determine the structure of a macromolecular crystal by using only electron diffraction data and the Sayre equation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electron diffraction method is a viable approach for the direct structure determination of protein structures.
the electron diffraction data can be used directly for structure determination, provided that the data are of sufficient quality and resolution.
the Sayre equation is a useful tool in the analysis of electron diffraction data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

electron crystallographic data are sufficiently rich in information to be able to solve protein structures directly, and that the information content of electron diffraction is sufficient for the direct structure solution of protein structures.
, with a few exceptions, it is not necessary to have a priori knowledge of the molecular symmetry in order to carry out electron crystallographic structure determination.
, with the proper data sets, it is possible to determine protein structures directly from electron crystallographic data.
